<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par135 />{{GHGmargin-letter|135|i}}
'''3.''' The ''oblique'' cases of the personal pronouns expressed by means of a preposition (or the ''nots accus.'' {{GHGheb|text=את}}) with a suffix may be used either in a demonstrative or reflexive sense,<ref>As in Luther’s Bible ''jm'' (''ihm''), ''jr'' (''ihr'') for ''sich'', and in our version ''him, her'' for ''himself, herself''.</ref> as {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ|translate=to him}}, but also ''to himself'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=16}} ''and Ehud made'' {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ|translate=for himself a sword}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=17}}; so also {{GHGheb|text=לָהֶם|translate=sibi}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֵלָיו|translate=unto him}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=9}} ''unto himself''; {{GHGheb|text=אִתּוֹ|translate=with him}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=3}} ''with himself''; {{GHGheb|text=עִמָּהּ|translate=with her}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=24}} ''with herself''; also apparently as a pleonastic ''dativus ethicus'' (see {{GHGpar|119|s}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=1|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|k}}
Rarely, and only when marked emphasis is intended, is the ''accusative'' of the reflexive pronoun represented by the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} {{GHGheb|text=את}} with a suffix (this being ordinarily expressed by the reflexive conjugations {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}<ref>{{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} according to {{GHGpar|51|e}} (like {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} according to {{GHGpar|54|f}}) may also include the ''dative'' of the reflexive pronoun.</ref>); thus, {{GHGheb|text=אֹתָם|translate=se ipsos}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=19}} in sharp antithesis to {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאֹתִי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=2}}, 8, 10. Cf. § 57 at the end, together with note 2.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|l}}
Rem. There is a similar emphasis in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=26}} on {{GHGheb|text=בְּשָׂרָם}} and {{GHGheb|text=דָּמָם}} in the sense of ''their own flesh, their own blood''. On the sometimes demonstrative, sometimes reflexive meaning of noun-suffixes of the 3rd person singular and plural, cf. § 91, p and q. For other circumlocutions to express the idea of ''self'', see {{GHGpar|139|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|m}}
'''4.''' The ''possessive pronouns'' are, according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}, expressed by the ''suffixes of the noun'' (in the genitive),<ref>Like the substantival genitive, according to {{GHGpar|129|h}}, the possessive pronoun may also be paraphrased by a relative clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=הַנְּעָרִים אֲשֶׁר לִי|translate=the young men, which}} are ''to me'', i.e. ''my young men''; so especially, when the substantive, which should take a genitive suffix, is already followed by a genitive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=40}}. In this case, however, the suffix also is sometimes attached pleonastically, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּרְמִי שֶׁלִּי|translate=my vineyard, which}} belongs ''to me.'' Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=7}}, and the analogous pleonasms in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=2}} (but see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=2}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=27|verse=2}}.</ref> which may represent either a ''subjective genitive'', or (like the genitives proper, {{GHGpar|128|h}}) an ''objective genitive'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֲמָסִי|translate=the wrong done against me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=35}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=13|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=21}}, &c.); 50:4, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=35|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=12|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲשֵׂ֫הוּ|translate=the treatment of him}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=56|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=6|hidebook=1}}. Cf. also such pregnant expressions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=20|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלַח עֶזְרְךָ|translate=he will send thy help}} (''help for thee''), i.e. he will send thee help; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=26}} (''and I will restore judges for thee''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=15}}.

When several substantives are co-ordinated, the pronominal suffix must be attached to each singly, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=36|verse=6}} ''and Esau took'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־נָשָׁיו וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וְאֶת־ בְּנֹתָיו|translate=his wives and his sons and his daughters}}, &c.; 38:18, &c. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=5}} the text is hardly correct.<section end=par135 /><noinclude>
